name: OSIsoft PI
tagline: The dominant industrial data historian: time-series storage plus asset context for plants and grids.
description: The PI System is an industrial data platform built around the PI Data Archive, a time-series historian that collects readings from control systems, PLCs and sensors through hundreds of interfaces, filters them with exception and swinging-door compression, and keeps decades of operational history online. PI Asset Framework adds an asset hierarchy, templates and calculations on top, and tools such as PI Vision and the PI DataLink Excel add-in put the data in front of engineers. OSIsoft, which built it from 1980, was acquired by AVEVA in March 2021 (AVEVA is itself owned by Schneider Electric), and it is now sold as AVEVA PI System, with PI Server 2024 R2 the current documented release and cloud services through AVEVA CONNECT. It is the default historian in process industries and utilities, but it is proprietary, Windows-based and priced for enterprises.
statusNote: OSIsoft was acquired by AVEVA in March 2021; the product is now marketed as AVEVA PI System.

pricing.notes: Sold through AVEVA subscription and enterprise agreements; pricing is not published.

scale.notes: Scales up per server; PI collectives provide high availability, and multi-site data is aggregated via PI-to-PI or AVEVA CONNECT.

strengths: De facto standard historian in oil and gas, power, chemicals and mining
Hundreds of connectors to PLC, DCS, SCADA and OPC sources
Exception and swinging-door compression keep decades of high-frequency data online
Asset Framework adds hierarchy, templates and calculations around raw tags
Familiar engineer tooling: PI Vision dashboards and the PI DataLink Excel add-in
weaknesses: Proprietary, Windows-based server stack with enterprise pricing
Lossy compression settings must be tuned up front or detail is gone for good
Tag-centric model and APIs feel dated next to SQL time-series databases
Bulk analytics usually means exporting to a data lake or warehouse
useCases: Plant and process historian for OT data
Grid, pipeline and utility network monitoring
Equipment condition monitoring and predictive maintenance feeds
notIdealFor: Developer-first apps wanting SQL and open formats
